What is Community-based Harassment?

Community-based harassment is a grown-up version of school yard bullying.Multiple individuals within a community participate in the harassment and stalking of a single individual. However, rather than attack a victim physically, techniques are used to undermine a person psychologically. This can be far more damaging than a physical attack because not only is it very hard to prove, but it is extremely traumatizing for the victim. (Also known as cause stalking or gang stalking).

What sets community-based harassment apart from the related examples to the right is that the reason it takes place is often obscure to the victim. Without a solid reason for its occurrence, victims are often dismissed as delusional.

In addition, this form of harassment often leaves the target a victim of ridicule among friends and family because of the subtle nature of the attacks, which further compounds the trauma to the victim. It is emotionally draining and isolating to the victims because it is extremely difficult to prove, and virtually impossible to prosecute.

For those of you whom haven't watched the episode I advise you do so before reading my comment as I like to analyze what happens in the episodes and will not refrain from discussing details of what happened. If you prefer to wait for the episodes to appear on youtube then enjoy a link to season 3 episode 1 (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_SP7vTgcMQY)

Not surprised that JNPR and SSSN won their matches, as the episode preview (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_SP7vTgcMQY) showed they'd be up against teams that we haven't met before so it would make sense that the teams more invested in the plot would advance.

For team JNPR we got to see Nora's semblance and it probably should have been a bit obvious what it was given how she's based off of Thor (for those unaware Ren is based off of Mulan, Phyrra on Achilles, and Jaune on Joan of Arc, making all members of team JNPR the opposite gender of the characters they're based off of). I personally was very pleased with Jaune's tactical skills, it was nice to see him using those again since they are the reason the Ozpin selected him as team leader (and probably the reason that Jaune even stayed in the school, as Godwin pointed out he was NOT ready for Beacon and this fact would not have been lost on Ozpin, Jaune demonstrating his leadership/tactical skills are probably the only reason he wasn't kicked out). However the conversation that happened after Jaune called for 'Flower Power', while likely for comedic effect, does show a bit of a failing to properly talk things out ahead of time (as say when Ruby called for say 'Checkmate' or the various other team attacks back in season 2 episode 4 no arguments were had). Since Jaune hasn't fully discovered his semblance (and for any who might have forgotten like I had, back in season 1 episode 14 we did see Jaune's semblance, the exact details of it however aren't fully known) and had a bit of issue with communication I doubt that he'll be making it to the doubles, while he might have tactical skills as there become fewer and fewer people in each match those tactical skills will become less valuable, relying more on a person's skills. While Ren certainly made a fair showing, Nora by far was the MVP of this match and for good reason, with Phyrra probably taking a close second, not to mention how she was able to hold off two opponents at least at once I think that the doubles match will be Phyrra and Nora. The biggest teamwork issue that I saw from JNPR was when it came to the team-attack discussion, so I don't think there will be a huge issue with Phyrra and Nora working together, but if it's not Phyrra and Nora then it'll probably be Ren and Nora as Jaune just isn't yet ready for these sorts of situations. That said, plot twists could obviously heavily influence things going different but that's just what I saw.

For team SSSN I think that it's worth pointing out for those who might not have been paying close attention, the big guy that got knocked out early was 'Sage' and the red haired pirate (voiced by Gavin Free) is 'Scarlet'. This fight I was hoping would have been able to help showcase team SSSN as not being rather weak as Sun and Neptune seemed to be in season 2 episode 4 (they were taken out VERY early), and I can't help but feel that this fight in general felt a bit sloppier than the other two fights that we've seen, while JNPR's fight definitely ended on a more 'humorous' note, a fair amount of team SSSN's match were these more humorous notes. Scarlet probably won't be making it to the next round I think, while he was able to hold his own at times and did help out, he was a bit clumsy (which I think fits well with the choice of voice actor) as seen where he almost got hit by those knives as well as a few other points during the fight, while Neptune was basically crippled by his fear (ironic given who he's probably based off of) said fear isn't that likely to appear in the doubles match (at least from the arena) while Scarlet being a clutz would. Sun is obvious a shoe in for the doubles round and probably even the single if they make it that far, he was very skilled and resourceful, able to hold his own and made no major mistakes, and he managed to help get Neptune to not be completely useless when the battle went to 'their' side. This leaves the other member of the doubles round between Sage and Neptune, while I kinda want to say Sage because Neptune's fear almost cost his team the match, Sage should have known that he needed to move when he was surrounded, nothing good could have come from standing there as we saw, and I feel that reflects shortcomings in his own skills, meanwhile Neptune didn't get knocked out and even took down three of the enemies despite his fear, so I hate to say it but I think that the doubles round will be Sun and Neptune (which does also fit in how season 2 had a fair amount of Sun and Neptune but this is the first time we're seeing Sage and Scarlet). It might go differently, but unless Sage has a fair amount of skill that he just didn't get a chance to showcase (because he didn't get out of the way!) I do think that Neptune showed that he'll be better for the next round. Though depending on who they're up against, Neptune's fear may be used against him (though perhaps not in the tournament even).

But those are just my thoughts. Will be interesting to see how what's going on with Winter and Weiss next episode...
